items.item_text: resume
cover letter
Certified culinary educator through the ACF or equivalent.
Food Protection Manager Certification or ability to obtain within first 6 months of employment (Preferred)
ANAB-Accredited Food Allergy Certificate (Preferred)
Bachelor's degree in Food Science, Nutrition, Public Health, Hospitality Management, and / or equivalent experience / training (Preferred)
Familiarity with adult-learning theory and/or previous experience training in a large-scale food service environment.
Prior experience in culinary food service operations.

Under the general direction of the Compliance & Food Safety Officer, the Culinary & Quality Assurance Trainer is responsible for training the trainer, providing hands-on training support and collaboration for new hire and existing support across the department to ensure food safety practices, occupational safety, and departmental and University standards are met. Reporting to the Compliance & Food Safety Officer, this position works closely with the Training Coordinator, Dietitian, Culinary and unit leadership, and other external stakeholders to provide hands-on training support across all dining units.
Training & Development - 40%

In collaboration with the Compliance & Food Safety Officer, Training Coordinator, and unit leadership, develop training materials and provide hands-on training to senior staff and supervisors in the unit. Provide spot training as needed during walkthroughs.

Serve as a subject-matter expert and provide instruction on knife skills, cooking techniques, station management, just-in-time cooking, speed/efficiency, plating standards, and other relevant culinary and food service training needs as identified and communicated by supervisor.
Conduct new hire culinary training, including food safety and operational procedures. Work with the Dietitian to ensure allergen training needs are addressed.
Facilitate ongoing skill development workshops based on operational standards, seasonal menus, culinary trends, or operational needs.
Evaluate staff performance and create individualized training plans to support growth in collaboration with unit and senior leadership.
Assess training programs regularly and make changes or improvements, as necessary.

In collaboration with the Training Coordinator, Dietitian, and Compliance & Food Safety Officer, and vendors or other external stakeholders to deliver food safety and other training to all levels of staff.
Culinary Quality & Standards - 35%
In collaboration with the Compliance & Food Safety Officer, conduct regular audits of culinary execution, product consistency, and station setup.
Ensure adherence to standardized recipes, portioning, and presentation across all dining locations.

Promote high standards of cleanliness, sanitation, and food safety in alignment with Berkeley Dinings HACCP plan(s) and local health regulations. Promote occupational safety standards to ensure work safety expectations and best practices are met. Provide spot-training as needed and make recommendations on additional corrective actions to unit leadership.
May support culinary leadership in testing and refining new recipes under a training lens; train the trainer on approved menu items and production methods. Perform spot training to staff, as needed.
Investigate non-compliance and/or potential concerns or issues as identified by the incumbent and/or the Compliance & Food Safety Officer.
Recommend standard policies or protocols to the Compliance & Food Safety Officer to address concerns.
Investigate and address food waste inconsistencies or the food waste gap in collaboration with the Sustainability Manager and Compliance & Food Safety Officer.
Operational Support - 10%
Collaborate with culinary leadership and unit managers to identify training gaps and operational inefficiencies.
Help implement workflow improvements and best practices for high-volume environments.
Serve as a resource for troubleshooting common operational challenges (equipment usage, production timing, menu transitions, etc.).

In collaboration with Compliance & Food Safety Officer, Dietitian, and The Hub, address missing service records, time and temperature logs, and overproduction/waste trends. Continue to train and reinforce as needed.

Under the oversight of the Compliance & Food Safety Officer, provide in-person support before and after location openings, collaborating with senior leadership and unit managers to ensure training and documentation needs are met; support training with new kitchen equipment, as needed; and ensure staff and trainers are equipped to open new locations with new recipes

Learn relevant kitchen management systems and software, including but not limited to Jamix, LeanPath, etc. May consult with the Hub on the development and planning of software and system trainings, as assigned.
Assist dining units during special events, as needed.
Leadership & Communication - 10%
Coach and mentor culinary staff to build confidence, teamwork, and professional growth.
Provide constructive feedback and encourage a positive kitchen culture rooted in learning and accountability.
Communicate training needs, progress, and outcomes to leadership teams.
Participate in staff meetings, menu planning sessions, and university dining initiatives.
Report disciplinary concerns and trends to the Compliance & Food Safety Officer and the unit leadership, as appropriate.
Promote a culture of safety, quality, hospitality, and accountability
Professional Development - 5%
Attendance at assigned meetings and trainings, completion of required trainings, professional development, and other duties as assigned.
General Industry, OSHA 30-Hour DOL Completion Card (Preferred)
Knowledge of commercial kitchen equipment and culinary techniques in high-volume environments.
Thorough knowledge of large-scale food production, including forecasting, preparation techniques, and cooking techniques at scale.
In-depth knowledge of food safety standards & ability to implement HACCP plans.
Ability to learn and adhere to Cal OSHA standards in 6 months and/or ability to obtain.
Ability to identify training gaps and make recommendations to address them.
Thorough verbal and written communication in the English language, active listening, dynamic flexibility, critical thinking, and the ability to multitask and ensure effective time management.
Thorough decision-making and reasoning skills, and the ability to develop original ideas to solve problems, including operations analysis and quality control analysis.
Thorough and effective interpersonal and work leadership skills to provide guidance to all levels of personnel.
Ability to work with diverse teams
Intermediate financial acumen demonstrating the ability to translate production techniques to financial savings.
Intermediate computer application skills.
